# Otok

> otok is a dependency manager for native C and C++ libraries. It builds each library from source on the user's
> machine, with the project's options, platforms, linkage and compiler, and writes them into one output directory for
> the app's build: XCFrameworks and a Swift package for Xcode and SwiftPM, `otok-config.cmake` for CMake, `otok.props`
> for Visual Studio, shared objects for Gradle. Targets: Apple (macOS, iOS and every other Apple platform and
> simulator), Android, Windows (MSVC or clang-cl) and Linux (GCC or Clang). Everything is declared in `otok.toml`;
> `otok.lock` pins every version, recipe and input by its hash. Recipes come from a public index
> (https://otok-dev.github.io/index/).

For coding agents:

- Pass `--format json` to the commands whose output you read: `search`, `info`, `outdated`, `audit`, `why` and
  `log --list` print one JSON document; `install`, `update` and `fetch` print JSON lines, one event per line, ending
  with `{"event":"end","exit":N}`. Errors and warnings are in `diagnostics` (or `diagnostic` events). Needs otok 0.5.34
  or later (`search` and `info`: 0.5.33).
- To add a library: `otok search <name> --format json`, then `otok info <recipe id> --format json` (versions,
  targets, options with their documentation), then a `[deps.<library>]` table in `otok.toml` with `recipe`, `version`
  and `options`, then `otok install --format json`.
- Edit `otok.toml`, never `otok.lock`. Commit both; `Otok/` is generated.
- The first install builds from source and can take many minutes; later ones use the machine's cache.
- A skill for agents (Agent Skills format, `SKILL.md`) with the whole workflow: `otok agent-skill` writes it into
  `.claude/skills/otok/` of the project (`--user`: `~/.claude/skills/`; otok 0.5.35 or later), or download
  https://otok-dev.github.io/skills/otok/SKILL.md

## Docs

- [Coding agents](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/agents/): how an agent drives otok, the skill and an `AGENTS.md` note
- [Install otok](https://otok-dev.github.io/start/install/): Homebrew, Scoop, the Linux install script, from source
- [First project for Apple](https://otok-dev.github.io/start/apple/): `otok.toml`, `otok install`, the Swift package
- [First project for Android](https://otok-dev.github.io/start/android/): the NDK, Gradle and CMake
- [First project for Windows](https://otok-dev.github.io/start/windows/): CMake and Visual Studio projects
- [First project for Linux](https://otok-dev.github.io/start/linux/): CMake, static or shared objects
- [Coming from CocoaPods](https://otok-dev.github.io/start/from-cocoapods/)
- [Options, linkage and profiles](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/options/)
- [Several targets in one project](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/targets/)
- [CMake projects with find_package](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/cmake/): the dependency provider
- [The lock and updates](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/lock/)
- [Continuous integration](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/ci/): `otok install --locked` and the cache
- [Tools for your own build](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/tools/)
- [Working on a library](https://otok-dev.github.io/guides/dev-builds/): building a library from its working tree

## Reference

- [Commands](https://otok-dev.github.io/reference/commands/): every command and option
- [otok.toml](https://otok-dev.github.io/reference/otok-toml/)
- [config.toml](https://otok-dev.github.io/reference/config/): the machine's settings
- [JSON output of the commands](https://github.com/otok-dev/otok/blob/main/docs/formats/cli-json.md): `--format json`
- [otok metadata](https://github.com/otok-dev/otok/blob/main/docs/formats/metadata.md): the project as JSON
- [The format documents](https://github.com/otok-dev/otok/tree/main/docs/formats): `otok.toml`, `otok.lock`,
  `recipe.toml`, `build.lua`, the index
